chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'Feeding a man from the Muslims is more beloved to me than feeding an 'Afqa' from the people.' I said, 'And what is the 'Afqa'?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'A hundred thousand, or more.'

key_terms.أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ: More beloved to me; indicates preference and spiritual merit.
key_terms.أُفُقاً: A term denoting a large multitude or crowd, specifically defined here as a hundred thousand people.
key_terms.مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: From the Muslims; referring to the specific community of believers.

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of feeding a Muslim compared to feeding a large crowd of people?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual superiority of feeding a single *Mu'min* (believer) over feeding a vast multitude ('Afqa'), defined as one hundred thousand people or more. This comparison underscores the Shia scholarly view that the intrinsic value of the recipient's faith and spiritual status outweighs the quantitative scale of the charity, reflecting the high esteem placed on the community of believers.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Feeding a man from the Muslims is more beloved to me than feeding an ‘Afqa’ from the people’. I said, ‘And what is the ‘Afqa’?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A hundred thousand, or more’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from certain individuals of our people from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Satisfying the hunger of a Muslim is more beloved to me than feeding a whole horizon of people.’ 1 then asked, ‘What is a horizon?’ The Imam said, ‘It is one hundred thousand or more people.’”
